claim.pdf_says: Sequential I-O - Input-Output Section (the running header at the top of the page, printed the same way as on every other page)
claim.why_it_matters: On every other page the transcription keeps the running header as plain text. Here it becomes a level-1 heading, which puts a false top-level division into the outline between SECTION VII and its subsection 2.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 380 (folio VII-6) prints 'Sequential I-O - Input-Output Section' at the top as an ordinary running header, in the same plain typeface as the body text, followed by the numbered heading '2. ENVIRONMENT DIVISION IN THE SEQUENTIAL I-O MODULE'. The transcription's page-380.md renders that running header as '# Sequential I-O - Input-Output Section'. The adjacent pages 379 and 381 keep their running headers as plain text. Across specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md, 54 running headers of the form 'Sequential I-O - ...' are plain lines; only this one (line 15354) and 'Relative I-O - File Description Entry' (line 17558) are promoted to '#'. Both sources quote the wording exactly the same, and no normative text changes. The defect is purely structural: a level-1 heading that is not in the standard enters the document outline above subsection 2, so outline-driven tools and readers see a false top-level division. That matches the claim's 'structural' severity.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as stated, but the defect is structural markup only: the header wording matches the PDF exactly. The same promotion also occurs at specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 17558 ('# Relative I-O - File Description Entry'), a sibling to sweep.
